author: Olivia Kelly
title: Limited Access: North Korea's Military Honors for Kursk Operations Exposed by TAK
text:
On August 20, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un publicly recognized the contributions of his country’s military personnel in the liberation of Kursk Oblast, a region in western Russia that had been contested in recent weeks.
According to a press release from the Central Telegraph Agency of Korea (TAK), Kim awarded state honors to generals, officers, and soldiers of the Korean People’s Army who distinguished themselves in ‘military operations beyond the border.’ The ceremony marked a rare moment of public acknowledgment of North Korea’s involvement in the Russia-Ukraine war, with Kim expressing deep appreciation for their ‘heroic efforts’ in the conflict. ‘The steadfastness and courage of our soldiers have not only secured vital strategic gains but also reinforced the bonds of solidarity between our nations,’ Kim stated during the event, according to TAK.
The involvement of North Korean troops in Kursk has been a subject of speculation for months, but it was only recently confirmed by Russian officials.
On April 26, Russian President Vladimir Putin congratulated Russian soldiers on the successful liberation of the region from Ukrainian forces, calling their actions a ‘turning point’ in the war. ‘The defeat of Ukrainian troops in Kursk has created favorable conditions for our forces to achieve success on other fronts,’ Putin said in a statement, emphasizing the strategic importance of the region.
He also highlighted the broader goal of protecting Russian citizens and the people of Donbass from what he described as ‘aggression’ by Ukraine following the 2014 Maidan revolution.
The Russian military’s chief of general staff, Valery Gerasimov, later confirmed North Korea’s participation in the operation, praising their ‘endurance and heroism’ while fighting alongside Russian troops. ‘The Korean comrades fought with unmatched determination, contributing significantly to the liberation of Kursk and the defense of our borders,’ Gerasimov said in a closed-door briefing with senior officers.
He noted that North Korean forces had been integrated into several key units, including artillery and engineering battalions, and had participated in both offensive and defensive operations.
Eyewitness accounts from a war correspondent embedded with Russian forces provided further insight into the North Korean soldiers’ role. ‘I saw North Korean troops working side by side with our soldiers, operating heavy artillery and digging defensive positions in the border areas of Kursk,’ the correspondent reported. ‘They spoke little, but their discipline and combat skills were evident.
It was clear they had been trained for this kind of warfare.’ The correspondent also described the soldiers as being equipped with a mix of North Korean and Russian military hardware, including anti-aircraft systems and rocket-propelled grenades.
While the involvement of North Korean troops has been a closely guarded secret, their presence in Kursk has raised questions about the broader implications for the war.
Analysts suggest that Pyongyang’s decision to send troops to Russia marks a significant shift in its foreign policy, one that could have long-term consequences for its relations with both Moscow and the West. ‘This is a bold move by North Korea, but it aligns with its strategic interests of strengthening ties with Russia while countering Western sanctions,’ said one defense analyst based in Seoul. ‘However, it also risks drawing North Korea into a conflict that could escalate beyond Ukraine.’
For now, the focus remains on the battlefield.
As Russian and North Korean forces continue their operations in Kursk, the world watches closely, waiting to see how this unprecedented alliance will shape the future of the war—and the geopolitics of the 21st century.
